rationale_evidence.anchor: Suppose K_t={p,q,r} but q is later discovered unsupported. Then K_{t+1}={p,r}. The cardinality decreased ... Yet epistemic quality may improve. ... |K_{t+1}|<|K_t| not=> K_{t+1} prec K_t.
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives a worked example (K_t={p,q,r} shrinking to K_{t+1}={p,r} after q is found unsupported) showing knowledge can improve while cardinality decreases, giving |K_{t+1}|<|K_t| does not imply K_{t+1} is epistemically worse -- the reason knowledge quantity and knowledge quality must remain separate.

rationale_evidence.anchor: A new observation can make the Gap **larger** without making KnowledgeOS worse. ... backup system is not actually verified ... The Gap increased. But epistemically, KnowledgeOS may have improved because an unknown problem became visible. GapIncrease not=> KnowledgeDecrease. The system has changed from Unknown to Known Gap. That is epistemic progress.
rationale_evidence.statement: States a profound consequence, worked with a backup-verification example: a new observation can enlarge the Gap (from Delta=empty because a requirement was not even represented, to Delta={backup verification} once it becomes known to be unmet) without making the system epistemically worse -- giving GapIncrease does not imply KnowledgeDecrease, since going from Unknown to Known-Gap is itself epistemic progress.
